newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open flat in quiet activity.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open flat in quiet activity.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened flat in quiet trade on Wednesday on the back of a stable Canadian dollar and scant interest in buying issues ahead of Friday's economic data, dealers said.

"The (Canada) dollar is still hanging in there, but we don't have much economic data to trade on. The market is taking a wait-and-see attitude," said one trader at a Canadian-based brokerage. "The market is definitely more upbeat than it was," the trader added.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill weakened to yield 3.13 percent from 3.13 percent at Tuesday's close.
Analysts said the fact that the Canadian dollar has held onto recent gains had helped to offset a bearish tone in the money market.
The Canadian dollar opened stronger on Wednesday at C$1.3722 (US$0.7288) after a round of interbank buying stirred the unit out of a quiet overnight range.
News that Canadian housing starts fell by 7.9 percent in June to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 140,200 from 152,300 in May failed to have a significant impact on the T-bill market.
"We're waiting for Friday's numbers," the trader said.
On Friday, Canada will release its labor force survey and the United States will report its producer prices index.
Analysts said both numbers would indicate the extent of economic growth in the two economies.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill was flat at a yield of 3.41 percent. The one-year T-bill dipped to yield 3.92 percent from 3.91 percent on Monday.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 3.15 percent, in the lower half of the Bank of Canada's 3.0-3.5 percent target range.
